papers.title: MRGPRX2 in Allergic and Immune-Mediated Diseases: Mechanisms, Clinical Relevance, and Therapeutic Translation
papers.authors: Reinisch W, Li Y, Xiong P, Li H, Pan Q, Wu C
papers.abstract: Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2) is a mast-cell-enriched receptor that mediates immunoglobulin E-independent activation by structurally diverse neuropeptides, host-defense peptides, microbial products, and selected cationic drugs. Its biology links tissue stress and neuroimmune signaling to degranulation, vascular responses, pruritus, barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory amplification, but the extent to which individual diseases depend on this pathway remains uncertain. The strongest clinical rationale begins with non-IgE-mediated immediate drug hypersensitivity, for which MRGPRX2 provides a direct mechanistic framework, although rocuronium illustrates the need to distinguish human MRGPRX2 pharmacology from murine Mrgprb2 and from IgE-mediated perioperative allergy. In atopic dermatitis, preclinical and human skin data support a potential amplifier role in type 2 inflammation and itch, but a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 did not demonstrate efficacy in an unselected population. In chronic urticaria, challenge, biomarker, and genetic studies suggest an MRGPRX2-responsive subgroup within a heterogeneous disease, whereas a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 in unselected chronic spontaneous urticaria was also negative despite earlier pharmacodynamic activity. Ulcerative colitis provides additional human tissue evidence for an MRGPRX2-associated mast-cell circuit, although murine Mrgprb2 studies show context-dependent protective and pathogenic effects. Emerging evidence in chronic prurigo, allergic contact dermatitis, asthma, mastocytosis, rheumatoid arthritis, synovial inflammation, and neurogenic inflammation is also considered, with explicit separation of human observations from mouse-model evidence. We integrate these findings with receptor pharmacology and early clinical development, emphasizing evidence hierarchy, validated biomarker needs, patient selection, tissue target engagement, safety, and trial design. Current data support MRGPRX2 as an investigational endotype-defining pathway rather than a universal driver of allergic or immune-mediated disease.

papers.title: Fatty acid-binding protein 2 suppresses liver metastasis by cytoplasmic sequestration of β-catenin to enhance ferroptosis sensitivity in colon cancer
papers.authors: Wu L, Wu H, Zhou Y, Ou G, Sun Y, Li X
papers.abstract: Metastatic colon cancer commonly exhibits resistance to ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation. However, the mechanisms linking metabolic regulation to ferroptosis during metastatic progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified fatty acid-binding protein 2 (FABP2) as a regulator associated with ferroptosis sensitivity and liver metastatic phenotypes in colon cancer. Multi-omics analyses of clinical specimens showed reduced FABP2 expression in advanced colon cancer, which was associated with metastatic progression and poor survival. Mechanistically, FABP2 interacted with β-catenin, altered its intracellular localization, and was associated with reduced β-catenin/TCF4-dependent transcription of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), a key regulator of ferroptosis resistance. FABP2 overexpression increased ferroptosis sensitivity, whereas FABP2 downregulation promoted GPX4-dependent ferroptosis evasion and metastatic phenotypes. Pharmacological inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling or GPX4 activity partially attenuated the effects of FABP2 loss. Together, these findings identify FABP2 as a factor associated with ferroptosis regulation and metastatic progression in colon cancer, and provide additional insight into the interplay between lipid metabolism, Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and ferroptosis.

papers.title: Prevalence and epidemiologic features of adult upper gastrointestinal Crohn's disease over the last 30 years: a scoping review
papers.authors: Lupas D, Natt N, Elzaanoun R, Yuan Y, Taylor P, Mortuza R
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Crohn's disease (CD) is an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract. Although upper gastrointestinal (UGI) manifestations are well recognized in pediatrics, UGI-CD in adults has historically been underestimated. Methodological limitations, including selective endoscopy and inconsistent classification, have contributed to variable prevalence estimates.
AIMS: Our goals were to summarize the prevalence of UGI-CD in adults with CD, understand demographic variations, and summarize knowledge gaps.
METHODS: We conducted a scoping review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL (1995-November 2025) using PRISMA-ScR and JBI methodology. Eligible studies reported adult UGI-CD prevalence or related epidemiologic data. Extracted variables included prevalence estimates, site-level involvement, and demographics. Systematic reviews were included to summarize review-level epidemiologic evidence.
RESULTS: In total, 117 primary studies and eight systematic reviews were included. Across 95 cohorts with prevalence data, the median prevalence of UGI-CD was 8.8% (IQR 3.99%-14.5%). Higher rates were observed in cohorts using systematic endoscopy and biopsy, while population-based cohorts reported lower values. Isolated UGI-CD was rare, with a median prevalence of 1.37% (IQR 0.87%-3.02%). Prevalence varied geographically and ethnically, with lowest rates in South Asian cohorts and higher rates in East Asian and Middle Eastern cohorts. Site-specific reporting was inconsistent, and few studies detailed modifiers such as smoking or family history.
CONCLUSIONS: Reported prevalence estimates of adult UGI-CD remain highly variable due to inconsistent definitions and detection strategies. Standardized, site-specific adult definitions and systematic diagnostic protocols are needed to enable cross-study comparisons and thus improve prevalence estimates and address demographic reporting gaps.
